back_translation: Blow the ram's-horn in Zion; sound the alarm on My holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants of the land tremble, for the Day of the LORD is coming; it is near—

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness. Like dawn spread over the mountains, a great and mighty people is coming; their like has never been before, nor will be again for ages to come.
Before them fire devours, and behind them a flame burns. The land before them is like the garden of Eden, but behind them a desolate wilderness—nothing escapes them.
Their appearance is like horses, and like war-horses they run.
They leap over the mountaintops with a noise like chariots, like the crackling of flame devouring stubble, like a mighty army drawn up for battle.
At the sight of them the peoples are in anguish; every face grows pale.
They charge like warriors; they scale the wall like soldiers; each marches straight on his way and does not swerve from his course.
They do not jostle one another; each goes on his own path; they burst through the weapons and are not halted.
They rush upon the city, run along the wall, climb into the houses, and enter through the windows like a thief.
Before them the earth quakes and the heavens tremble; the sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withhold their shining.
The LORD utters His voice before His army; His camp is very great, and mighty are those who carry out His command. For the Day of the LORD is great and very terrible—who can endure it?
The LORD declares, 'Yet even now, return to Me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.'
Rend your hearts and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for He is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, abounding in steadfast love, and He relents from punishment.
Who knows—He may turn and relent and leave behind Him a blessing, a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
Blow the ram's-horn in Zion; consecrate a fast; proclaim a solemn assembly.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation; call the elders to assemble; gather the children, even nursing infants. Let the bridegroom come out of his room, and the bride from her bridal chamber.

Let the priests who minister to the LORD weep between the porch and the altar, and say, 'Spare Your people, O LORD; do not make Your heritage an object of scorn, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, "Where is their God?"'
Then the LORD became jealous for His land and had pity on His people.
The LORD answered His people: 'Behold, I am sending you grain, new wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied; and I will no longer make you an object of scorn among the nations.'

I will drive the northern army far from you, banishing it into a dry and desolate land; its vanguard into the eastern sea and its rear into the western sea. Its foul stench will rise, its reek will ascend, because it has done great things.
O land, do not fear; be glad and rejoice, for the LORD has done great things.
O wild animals, do not fear, for the pastures of the wilderness have turned green again; the tree bears its fruit, the fig tree and the vine yield their abundance.

O children of Zion, be glad and rejoice in the LORD your God, for He has given you the early rain for your vindication; He has poured down for you abundant rain, both the early rain and the latter rain, as before.
The threshing floors will be full of grain, and the vats will overflow with new wine and oil.
I will restore to you the years that the locusts have eaten—the swarming locust, the hopping locust, the destroying locust, and the cutting locust—My great army that I sent among you.
You will eat in plenty and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wondrously with you; and My people will never again be put to shame.
You will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God and there is no other; and My people will never again be put to shame.
